title: 微软申请「广告积分」系统专利，可在 PC 和 Xbox 上不打断游戏体验地展示广告
content:
Microsoft files patent for "ad-credit" system to show ads on PC and Xbox without disrupting gameplay | GamesIndustry.biz

.
Microsoft has patented an "ad-credit" system to display adverts and announcements during PC and Xbox game sessions without disrupting gameplay.
The patent, titled 'Contextually Aware Management of Interactive Software Application Access,' was
filed earlier this month
(as spotted by
Respawn First
).
The system is said to identify natural pauses, such as loading screens, menus, or the end of missions and rounds, before pausing the game to display an advertisement. During the ad, gameplay and controls would be temporarily suspended to ensure players do not lose progress.
After viewing the content, players would receive a "credit" to grant a period of ad-free play, ranging from 15 minutes to an hour or more.
The patent also indicated that uninterrupted playtime may be "defined at least partially by progression or events in game, such as five rounds of gameplay, completing one level, completing three online multiplayer matches, defeating an NPC, or completing a project or task."
In 2022, reports emerged that Xbox was
considering in-game advertisements for free-to-play titles
on its cloud streaming platform. Microsoft began
testing ad-supported game streaming on Xbox
this July.
Xbox Insider Program participants can opt for free, one-hour game streaming sessions supported by ads, which appear before each session. Core gameplay remains unchanged.
Earlier this month, Xbox announced
monthly cloud gaming limits for Game Pass subscribers
in November 2026.
Game Pass Essential will be limited to five hours, Premium to ten hours, and Ultimate to fifteen hours per month. Subscribers will be able to purchase additional cloud playtime through the Xbox Store once these limits are reached.
Xbox said it made the decision because "the cost of providing cloud gaming grows as more people use it and play for longer."
This week,
Xbox announced additional layoffs
as part of
its ongoing restructuring
. A total of 268 positions were affected at Halo Studios, other first-party developers, and Xbox Game Studios.
UK studio Rare and Age of Empires developer World's Edge have been transferred to Activision, which will also manage the Halo franchise.
Obsidian has moved under Bethesda, while Playground Games and Turn 10 have merged into a single studio.
